claims.text: On November 5, 2026, Google Cloud announced the donation of Agent Substrate, gVisor, and OpenRL to the CNCF, following their acceptance into the CNCF Sandbox the previous month.
Agent Substrate reached its 1.0 milestone and became generally available as Agent Substrate on GKE.
Agent Substrate decouples stateful agent sessions and identities from active compute, snapshotting idle agents to storage and restoring them in under 500 milliseconds.
Agent Substrate is claimed to run millions of sandboxes at 10x container density.
OpenRL orchestrates self-hosted reinforcement-learning post-training loops in plain Python on Kubernetes, across millions of parallel sandboxed rollouts.
Public development of Agent Substrate started in May 2026, and the project has grown to more than 100 contributors; gVisor is on a path toward CNCF Incubation.
Tessl, a New York AI-native software development firm, launched an open standards platform for building software factories, reported on November 6 and 8, 2026.

Mastra Factory, an open-source factory server connecting GitHub, Linear, and Slack to a configurable board (intake, triage, planning, build, review, done), has been in beta since September 2026 and installs with `npm create factory`.
According to Mastra's September 2026 beta announcement, its factory writes 25-35% of Mastra's PRs and closes 50-60% of its issues.
Overalls, Geoffrey Huntley's self-hosted platform of persistent Firecracker microVMs (formerly loom) with Claude Code and Codex preinstalled, is a research preview launching November 2026.
OpenAI AgentKit / Agent Builder is shutting down in November 2026.
LeadDev's September 2026 article by Chris Kelly describes three factory production lines (PR to merge, ticket to PR, alert to resolution), with a case study of 728 PRs in two weeks.

Dex Horthy argued at AI Engineer World's Fair (July 2026) that lights-off software factories fail because models cannot yet judge codebase maintainability, and recommended heavier upfront planning with humans still reading the code.
A September 2026 Dev Interrupted roundtable covered who owns PRs, measuring cost per effective merged PR and rework, and incident response as the last frontier for software factories.
Steve Yegge's August 2026 'Fences, not Sandboxes' describes Wheelhouse, a software factory that grew its own constitutional governance in place of technical sandboxes.
A four-layer software-factory architecture (compute, dev environment, harness, orchestration) was presented in the August 2026 'ai that works' podcast by Vaibhav Gupta and Dex Horthy.
Stripe's homegrown coding agents were reported to merge over a thousand PRs a week with humans still reviewing.
Zalando open-sourced an identity broker letting AI agents act for users without holding their provider tokens, using a delegation-chain design and user-agent permission intersection model.
A Danish team's software factory write-up concluded that context and measurable standards matter far more than code generation.
NVIDIA released an agent sandbox runtime with kernel-level enforcement, credentials injected only for approved endpoints, and formal verification of policy changes.
Anthropic built a new source control system called Scion after Git could not keep up with merges on its monorepo (roughly 30,000 merges in September).
The Pi agent reached version 1.0.0 with MCP support, and a variant, Pi Durable, was designed for long-running tasks.
DeepSeek released an open-source harness (dsh) in public preview in which everything is a plug-in.

On November 4, 2026, NVIDIA published its Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX), a reference architecture for a factory manager agent using Nemotron, the NemoClaw harness, and OpenShell, coordinating Visual Inspection, Fleet Management, and Root Cause Analysis agents.
On November 3, 2026, PagerDuty introduced Paige, an SRE agent that writes each incident resolution back into shared memory and drafts post-incident reviews.
